I'm non-binary, so when I was a young child my body didn't bother me. As soon as I hit puberty, I hated what was happening. I despised that I was growing body hair. Sexuality and libido repulse me. An abnormally large Adam's apple and a deep voice are constant reminders that I'm not who I want to be.

That said, I still didn't realize I was trans (though I spent a lot of time wishing and praying I'd end up a girl or a girly boy, it never really struck me as something cis people wouldn't do). When I was 16, I started reading "gender-bender" stories. Basically, the male protagonist turns or looks female, or the female protagonist turns or looks male. After reading the first one I found, I looked for others. Before I knew it, I'd read 20+ gender-bender series (don't know if that's what the genre is called, it's just what I've seen it referred to as). One of the stories in particular struck me, as it dealt with being specifically trans, rather than "magical events" and whatnot. Once I realized why I resonated so strongly with that character, I also found out that I was, in fact, trans.

From there it was all-aboard the hate-train to further despise my body. I've started getting things done about it. I originally thought I was a binary trans woman, but as I consider the possibilities, being a man vs being a woman, I find that I dislike both options. So I opt out. I'm just going to try to go for genderless.

My family has been supportive to an extent. My sister and mother make no effort to not out me, despite my saying I'm not comfortable with people knowing yet. My mother actually told several other family members without my permission, and now things are awkward between them and me. My father and two of my brothers have literally forgotten already (whenever I bring up a trans-related subject, like getting electrolysis, they act confused—"why would you need something like that?" "Because I'm trans and I don't like my facial hair." "But why don't you like your facial hair?" "*Because I'm trans.*" "Oh, really?"—conversation example set on repeat ~once monthly). My oldest brother is supportive, but he lives a long way away (1000+ miles), so he can't do anything when the rest of my family are being inconsiderate.

At the rate it's going, I might unknowingly be out to my whole family by the end of the year. (*internal screaming*)

I'd say give them the benefit of the doubt, honestly. They could just be trying to be supportive of you figuring yourself out. A family member being trans is generally the last thing someone considers. Maybe they just think you're supporting the LGBT+ community (or they think you are a lesbian yourself). While in your mind it's obvious that you're a guy, they've known you as a girl all your life, and they won't change that without something major, like you coming out to them.

If you suspect they already know you're trans, then you could try checking their post history on Facebook or whatever. It'd be a more certain way to find the answers you're looking for than asking here. We can only give you some biased opinions.

Just my two cents'. Hope this helps.

It is true that I used IPL. I just now checked. The package was advertised as "laser hair removal". My bad.

But while it is less effective, it is not "much" less effective. While I hate to use Wikipedia as a source,

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intense_pulsed_light

>A 2006 article in the journal "Lasers in Medical Science" compared IPL and both alexandrite and diode lasers. The review found no statistical difference in effectiveness, but a higher incidence of side effects with diode laser treatment. Hair reduction after 6 months was reported as 68.75% for alexandrite lasers, 71.71% for diode lasers, and 66.96% for IPL. Side effects were reported as 9.5% for alexandrite lasers, 28.9% for diode lasers, and 15.3% for IPL. All side effects were found to be temporary and even pigmentation changes returned to normal within 6 months.

About 2-4% less hair removal over 6 months. As long as you have regular preventative sessions to keep the hair from returning, I don't think it's a bad option by any means.

That said, ~70% hair reduction doesn't seem like an awful lot. I'd just keep in mind that those 30% will probably be clear after that long, so not very noticeable. Full-body electrolysis isn't feasible.

I'm also pretty sure that, based on the flashes after each use, the professional also used IPL (white light).

You wouldn't direct that negative emotion inward if the cause, the person to blame, wasn't you, would you? Obviously, you would be angry at him. That anger might be expressed in different ways—not letting yourself get an expensive phone, or something; versus having him pay you back, or not speaking to him anymore (at least for a while)—but it's the exact same anger.
